title: Static Methods, Getters, and Setters
objective: Define a static factory method, and a getter/setter pair that guards how a property can be set.

sourceAlignment.title: JavaScript Crash Course
sourceAlignment.author: Nick Morgan
sourceAlignment.note: Alignment metadata only. Lesson prose and exercises are original Code Forge material.

paragraphs: A static method belongs to the class itself, not to any instance. You call it as ClassName.method(...), never on an instance, which makes it a natural place for a factory function — one that builds and returns a new instance for you, often with some setup already applied.

A getter looks like a plain property from the outside (instance.value, no parentheses) but actually runs a method behind the scenes whenever it's read. Write one with get propertyName() { return ...; } inside a class.

A setter is the write-side equivalent: instance.value = x looks like plain assignment, but runs a set propertyName(x) { ... } method instead. This lets you validate or adjust a value on the way in — for example, refusing to let it go below zero — without the code that assigns it looking any different from a normal property assignment.
explanation.rule: static makes a method belong to the class itself; get/set let instance.property reads and writes run real code behind ordinary-looking property syntax.

examples.title: A Static Factory and a Guarded Setter
examples.note: Battery.empty(100) is a static factory — called on the class, not an instance. Setting level to 150 runs the setter, which clamps it down to 100 (the capacity), so the getter reads back 100.

checks.question: class Robot { static build() { return new Robot(); } } — how do you call build()?

feedback.correct: Correct — a static method belongs to the class itself, so you call it as ClassName.method(), never on an instance.
feedback.incorrect: static methods live on the class itself, not on any instance — call it as Robot.build().

assignment.title: Battery Pack
assignment.brief: Write a Battery class: constructor(capacity) storing capacity and an internal level starting at 0; a level getter/setter where the setter clamps the value between 0 and capacity; and a static full(capacity) method returning a new Battery already set to its capacity. Then write runBatteryDemo(capacity) that creates a battery with Battery.full(capacity), tries setting level to capacity + 50, and logs the resulting level.
requirements: Define class Battery with constructor(capacity) storing capacity and an internal level (starting at 0).
Define a level getter and a level setter that clamps the assigned value between 0 and capacity.
Define a static full(capacity) method that returns a new Battery with level already set to capacity.
Define runBatteryDemo(capacity) using Battery.full(capacity), setting level to capacity + 50, then logging level.
assignment.outputCheckLabel: runBatteryDemo(100) logs 100 (overcharge attempt clamped by the setter)

hints: The setter should use Math.max(0, Math.min(this.capacity, value)) to clamp value into range.
static full(capacity) can build a Battery and then use its own setter (battery.level = capacity) to fill it.
Battery.full(capacity) is called on the class itself, not with new Battery.full(...).
capacity + 50 exceeds the capacity, so the setter should clamp it back down to exactly capacity — 100 for this test.
